messages:
alex: quick proposal — hybrid per-tenant credit allocator + local token-bucket on each shard. credits are a soft global budget (periodic allotment). shards can borrow up to a configurable limit from neighbors. goal: reduce head-of-line blocking and avoid global rejects during short spikes.

sofia: sketch sounds useful. can you spell out the interface between admission service and shard limiter? what signals are forwarded?

alex: admission assigns credits (int tokens) + a policy version and priority class. response headers: X-Quota-Credit, X-Quota-Expiry, X-Admission-Policy. shard checks local token-bucket first, then consults local ledger for credits; if exhausted, it attempts peer-borrow, else applies fallback (reject/queue/degrade).

kevin: how do we avoid cross-shard races when many shards try to borrow for same tenant? that seems latency-sensitive.

alex: keep transfers best-effort and bounded. use a small deterministic ring coordinator per-tenant for arbitration and CAS-style ledger ops. allow transient negative credits up to borrow_limit to avoid synchronous stalls. borrow is optimistic + reconciled asynchronously.

taylor: what telemetry do we expose for SLOs/alerts? need quick signal for runaway borrowing.

alex: metrics: credits_allocated, credits_used, borrow_events, borrow_latency_ms, borrow_failures, rejects_by_policy. tag by tenant, shard, and policy_version. add alert when borrow_failures > threshold or borrow_latency_p95 > 200ms.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: planned canary deploy on eng-infra-canary at 2026-04-01T09:00Z :robot_face:

sofia: tradeoffs: more cross-shard state + complexity vs fewer false positives and better tail latency. borrow_limit sizing critical. we should default conservative.

kevin: what about tenant tiers? enterprise/prod/free should have clear precedence but avoid starving free tier entirely. maybe probabilistic smoothing?

alex: agree. policy sketch below. enterprise gets higher weight and borrow_limit; free has small borrow headroom and probabilistic admission during congestion.

alex: policy example:
```
admission:
  tiers:
    enterprise:
      weight: 100
      borrow_limit: 500
    prod:
      weight: 50
      borrow_limit: 200
    free:
      weight: 10
      borrow_limit: 20
credit_allocation:
  window_sec: 60
  default_tokens_per_window: 1000
```

sofia: implementation boundary suggestion: admission service owns global allocation and policy, exposes a compact REST API: POST /allocations {tenant, window_id} -> {tokens, window_id, policy_version}. shards own local ledger and peer-borrow RPCs (or call coordinator). keep admission stateless-ish and versioned.

kevin: rollback plan? how do we revert if borrow logic causes regressions?

alex: rollout plan: 1) opt-in dev tenants (no borrow) 2) 5% canary with passive metrics 3) enable borrow with borrow_limit=low for 1% traffic 4) increase to full with autoscaler tuning. fallback: admission supports "passthrough" mode (X-Admission-Mode: passthrough) to preserve old behavior.

taylor: how do we handle abuse detection? needs to short-circuit borrowing for malicious tenants.

alex: abuse detection tags tenants async. when flagged, admission sets borrow_limit=0 and adds penalty windows; shards enforce hard caps and route to quarantine variants or return 429 with retry-after. keep an "emergency" metric stream to surface these events.

sofia: sounds good. i'll draft an RFC follow-up with diagrams and an interface appendix. will ping for review after lunch. :thumbsup:
